title: The four infrastructure walls
question: Why does adding accelerators expose different infrastructure limits?
scope: The four configuration-specific examples illustrate distinct limits; they do not predict a universal bottleneck.

steps.title: Feed arithmetic
steps.description: The narrow HBM connection feeds the FP8 arithmetic block. Peak arithmetic is useful only when the workload supplies enough reuse per byte.

steps.title: Power the rack
steps.description: The DGX H100 bar exceeds the traditional rack reference. More compute density requires a compatible electrical and cooling envelope.

steps.title: Cross the node boundary
steps.description: The NVLink and InfiniBand bars expose different per-direction bandwidth budgets. A collective crossing nodes cannot assume local-link bandwidth.

steps.title: Accumulate failure exposure
steps.description: The fleet bar uses independent failures: more GPUs shorten the interval between fleet interruptions even when each GPU is individually reliable.

title: Elastic training worker lifecycle and state machine

steps.title: Maintain one active group

title: ML system attack surface

scope: This taxonomy identifies entry points, not probabilities or proof that every entry compromises every layer.

infra.label: Infrastructure container and incoming threat paths

steps.title: Inspect incoming records
steps.description: Poisoned records and backdoor triggers enter through training data. Data provenance and validation address this boundary.

steps.title: Inspect code and artifacts
steps.description: Imported packages affect training execution, while weight theft and unsafe loading affect model artifacts. These are different trust decisions.

steps.title: Inspect exposed queries
steps.description: The serving API permits extraction, adversarial inputs, and membership-inference attempts through interactions with the deployed system.

steps.title: Inspect the supporting platform
steps.description: Hosts, network, firmware, drivers, schedulers, and keys underpin the upper layers. A model-only defense leaves these dependencies outside its scope.

title: Threat prioritization matrix
question: How should likelihood and impact influence defense priorities?
scope: Point locations are qualitative judgments; changed context can move a threat without changing its name.

steps.title: Prioritize recurring severe exposure
steps.description: Data poisoning in federated training appears in the upper-right quadrant, motivating automated defenses for the illustrated threat model.

steps.title: Condition hardware risk on access
steps.description: Hardware side channels start at lower likelihood, but the dashed arrow shows how exposed hardware or sensitive co-tenants can change that judgment.

steps.title: Condition privacy impact on data
